tei:titleStmt.tei:title: נִשְׁמַת שְׁדוּדִים
Nishmat Shedudim — reshut No3 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Divrei

tei:div.tei:head: Nishmat Shedudim — reshut No3 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Divrei

tei:lg.tei:l: The soul of shaken, taken ones in tyrant lands convening
laud You year after year, pronouncing keening.
The words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, of the priests. (Jeremiah 1:1)
The soul of mutineers at Anathoth’s mouth unheard
praise You year after year, recalling their rebuker’s word,
The words of the Cause who sent him.
The soul of upset ones who set their hearts toiling in fear
exalt You, not hearing together, sealed is their ear.
The words of the prophets, with one mouth. (I Kings 22:12)
The soul of entrapped ones in their sin’s trap and net
hymn You who will herald complete comfort-words yet!
The soul of low-down rogues in rebellion failing
sing of You, speaking to You at the time of their wailing:
And were our mouths as full of song as the sea...

tei:note.tei:p: Israel, who rebelled against the word of Jeremiah, from Anathoth

Note that most printings read דְּבַר “the word of” in the singular here. This is not the form found in Exodus, nor is it parallel to the other concluding verses, all of which start with דִּבְרֵי, so it has been emended here.
The introductory line to the second part of Nishmat, and the standard conclusion for a Nishmat reshut.
